walkthrough:
**Spot what the enzyme is made from**

This enzyme is not one chain, it is two identical chains of 99 amino acids working together.

Whenever two or more polypeptides join to make a working protein, that is quaternary structure, so quaternary must be involved.

**See how the active site is built**

In each chain, only amino acids 25, 26 and 27 form part of the active site.

Which amino acids sit at those positions is decided by the sequence, so that is primary structure. How that chain coils, folds and holds those three amino acids in exactly the right 3D position is secondary and tertiary structure.

**Put it all together**

The final active site needs the correct amino acids (primary), correctly folded in each chain (secondary and tertiary), and the two chains correctly fitted together (quaternary).

That means all four levels control the shape, which is option A.

options.A: Correct, because primary sets the sequence including positions 25-27, secondary and tertiary fold each chain, and quaternary joins the two chains to make the complete active site.
options.B: This misses quaternary, but the active site is formed from two separate chains joining, so quaternary is essential.
options.C: This misses secondary and tertiary, but each 99 amino acid chain must coil and fold to bring positions 25-27 into the correct 3D shape.
options.D: Quaternary alone is not enough, because without the correct sequence and folding, the right amino acids would not be in the right place to form the active site.
